mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicate a weakening consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to adopt an accommodative monetary policy, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced manufacturing output and potential economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1,200,000 units, it indicates a contraction in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1200.0, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS is stable or rising, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high residential sales (RSAFS > 750,000), consumer spending on housing is robust, which is a leading indicator of strong economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 750000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
